confirmed.suspectedCause: src/content/adapters/youtube.ts (home and search extract, around lines 375 and 473) does blocks.push(shortsBlock(shorts, …)) after the result list. So the Shorts section always comes after an endless list. Reaching it starts loading more, which pushes it down. Putting the section where the original's shelf is (inline at its index), or above the list, would keep it still.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on the live site. Search 'rick astley', using real wheel steps (shortsreach.ts with my own tab). Three rounds where the collapsed Shorts section reached the screen: top 714 went to 4103 within 4 s (li 40 to 80), 715 went to 3964 (li 80 to 118), and 764 went to 3790 (li 118 to 153). Home did the same: 715 went to 2760 after 0.5 s (li 117 to 141). The original, read from the same DOM, has its Shorts shelves inline at rows 8, 12, 24 and 27 of 44 (grid-shelf-view-model). Sift folds every shelf into one section after ol.items. Mouse clicks miss. With PRE=2000, the click aimed at /shorts/5Dj2DppA4aI (y 446) landed on the 'Don't Say Goodbye' result after the target moved to y 1219, and watch?v=X6uzlX51kbo&list=RD… opened. With the default 300 ms pause I ran it twice: once the target moved to y 573 and the click hit a metadata line (nothing opened), and once it moved to y 769 and watch?v=X6uzlX51kbo opened. The code agrees. youtube.ts home() at line 375 and results() at line 473 push shortsBlock after the items block. nudgeEnd in index.ts loads more whenever the view is within 1.5 screens of the end, and a section that comes last is always that close. So a mouse user cannot reach the section until the feed runs out, and a click often opens a different video. No earlier rejected.md covers it. This is a real usability bug, medium to high.
confirmed.fix: In src/content/adapters/youtube.ts home() (line ~375) and results() (line ~473), stop pushing shortsBlock(...) after the items block. Insert it before the feed/results items block (after Topics or chips), or split the items list at the index of the original's first Shorts shelf. Then infinite loading never moves the section.

confirmed.suspectedCause: The model's line fails one of the line checks (vetLine or lineFits in src/background/index.ts), and KEEP_TITLE is saved, so the title stays for 30 days. One possible gap I found offline: unsupported() flags 'Never answer these 5 questions…' as an unsupported number when the title writes 5 as the Persian digit '۵'.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced. On an English home load (lang en/en), 3 of 21 entries showed only a foreign title with no English line: 'اخبار بامدادی | سهشنبه ۵ آبان', 'کلاهبرداری که فلیم حسین رو ۱.۲ میلیارد دونیت کرد…' and 'Радіодиктант національної єдності 2026 | Дивіться НАЖИВО на Суспільному'. All four of their cache entries, plus the Chinese one, were '\0keep-title' with no exp field. That means save() wrote them after a failed check (30 days), not the one-day refusal path. I found the check T1 missed. I deleted those four entries, hooked the worker's fetch and reloaded. The model (openai/gpt-6-luna, the fallback) answered 'Persian morning news for Tuesday, 5 Aban', a good English line, and Sift stored keep-title again. Offline, unsupported() returns 'number' for that line, for 'Never answer these 5 questions…' against '۵', and for '1.2 billion' against '۱.۲'. numbersOf/sourceNumbers in src/background/text.ts match digits with \d, which in JS is ASCII 0-9 only. So a title written with Persian or other non-ASCII digits has no numbers, and any line that repeats its number is dropped. The Ukrainian entry fails for a different reason: the model answered in Ukrainian ('Національний радіодиктант єдності 2026 наживо…'). lineFits rightly rejected it, but keep-title is then cached for 30 days with no retry. The Chinese entry got an English line this time, so its earlier keep-title was model variance. The original shows the same titles, so nothing is lost. But those entries miss the one-line description in the page's language that the spec asks for, and the digit bug is deterministic and sticks for 30 days. Medium, at the low end.
confirmed.fix: In src/background/text.ts, normalize non-ASCII decimal digits (\p{Nd}: Persian ۰-۹, Arabic-Indic ٠-٩, Devanagari, full-width and others) to ASCII before numbersOf/sourceNumbers/LISTED match. Or match \p{Nd} and map it with its code-point offset. Then unsupported() in vetLine finds '۵' and '۱.۲' in the source. Separately, in doLines (src/background/index.ts ~line 568-578), when lineFits fails for the wrong language, ask the next model in the chain once, or save KEEP_TITLE with a short TTL instead of 30 days.

confirmed.verdict: Confirmed in part. Severity is medium, not high. The core reproduces on the home page and on the article. Sift's header is 'Cerca in Corriere | Cerca | Menu'. No a or button in Sift matches /accedi|login|abbonati/. The Menu dialog (2274 characters) has no sign-in entry. The original header shows a.button--login 'Accedi' at 1096,20, 115x19 (home) and 1161,13 (article). It is visible, inside header.header--topbar. The link is dropped because its label fails TOP_LABEL (~6789), which knows only English, Spanish and Portuguese words. I ran the regex: 'Accedi' false, 'Se connecter' false, 'Connexion' false, 'Anmelden' false, 'Sign in' true. One part of the claim is a harness artifact: the dialog route works. After SALVA, the page view also shows a second 'ACCEDI' button under the first story, behind the dialog's backdrop. act.ts click:ACCEDI picks the first match in document order, so it clicked that hidden copy. With the dialog's own button ('[role=dialog] button.btn'), Sift went to https://www.corriere.it/account/login?landing=https://www.corriere.it/. So that route works, but only through a story's SALVA dialog. The visible header sign-in is still missing on Italian pages, and the same gap likely hits French and German sites. Side note, not claimed: the duplicate 'ACCEDI' that appears in the page view after SALVA looks like a separate small extraction bug.

A javascript: link already becomes a ref-only action through toAction, and act() replays it with proxy.click.

confirmed.title: BBC Anthropic article: Short version loses section '2.' and files the loss figures under '3. But luckily it has plenty of cash on hand'
confirmed.evidence: The full text has H2s '1. Armageddon is an occupational hazard', '2. The company is haemorrhaging cash', '3. But luckily it has plenty of cash on hand', '4.…' and '5.…'. The Short version's headings are 1, 3, 4, 5. Under '3. But luckily it has plenty of cash on hand' it shows a list item 'Anthropic is losing money' and then the $2 trillion valuation and $80.7bn loss paragraphs (section 2's content). After that comes a list item 'It has substantial cash, but high costs'. The model-made sub-items ('AI could pose catastrophic risks', 'Anthropic is losing money', 'It has substantial cash…') are each a one-item ol with no start, so each is drawn as '1.'. A reader of '5 surprising things' sees 1, 3, 4, 5 and losses under a 'plenty of cash' heading. The numbers themselves match the source (ratio 0.47). Shots: /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r12t2-bbc-anth-short-h3.png, /home/nico/projects/sift-test-2/research/shots/r12t2-bbc-cwn8d7g29vd9o-600.png
confirmed.repro: SIFT_PORT=9462 SIFT_TAB=T2-news bun scripts/act.ts goto:https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwn8d7g29vd9o wait:15000 'eval:[...document.querySelector("sift-root").shadowRoot.querySelectorAll("main h2, main ol > li")].map(h=>h.localName+": "+h.innerText.slice(0,50))'  → h2 1., li, h2 3., li 'Anthropic is losing money', li, h2 4., h2 5. Then click:Show full text and list the h2s again → 1 to 5.
confirmed.suspectedCause: The model dropped heading 2's placeholder and wrote its own numbered sub-points. The Markdown renderer also drops ordered-list start numbers (ol without start), so '2. …' and '3. …' show as '1.'.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced from the cached Short version. The Short version's h2s are '1. Armageddon…', '3. But luckily it has plenty of cash on hand', '4.…' and '5.…'. Section 2 'The company is haemorrhaging cash' is missing. Under heading 3 come the item 'Anthropic is losing money', then the $2 trillion valuation paragraph, the $80.7bn loss paragraph and the Hooper paragraph, then the item 'It has substantial cash, but high costs'. Each of those items is a separate <ol> with no start, drawn as '1.' (list-style decimal; shot checked). 'Show full text' and the original both list h2s 1 to 5. Reading the code supports both mechanisms. In short.ts planShort, a source heading the model dropped is put back before the next anchor (heading 3). The model's text for section 2 sits after heading 3, so the restored heading 2 has nothing under it, and the 'heading with nothing under it' pass removes it. In ui/markdown.tsx, ordered items render as <ol><li> and lose the model's number (line ~121 matches /^\s*\d+[.)]\s+/ but keeps no start). The result misfiles losses under a 'plenty of cash' heading and skips a number in a numbered listicle. Medium.
confirmed.fix: src/content/short.ts planShort: when a dropped source heading would land with no text before the next heading, place it before the first text segment whose pos is in the range of that heading's section (pos between heading i and the next heading), even when that segment comes after the next heading. Or move that text segment up under the restored heading instead of deleting it in the empty-heading pass. src/content/ui/markdown.tsx: keep the first item's number as <ol start={n}> when it is not 1.

confirmed.title: Corriere (Italian page): Sift's own UI strings fall back to English
confirmed.evidence: Page and view lang are it-IT. Some Sift labels are Italian: Cerca, Mostra testo completo, Versione breve, Vista Sift. Others are English: the skip button 'Skip to content', and the audio portal's name 'Interactive area from the original page: Example · widget.spreaker.com. Press Enter to use it, Tab to leave.' In src/content/i18n.ts the it table has 42 of the 99 keys of the en table. The 57 missing keys include skip, back10, fwd10, mute, unmute, video, interactive, enterToUse, shortening, shortReady, error, next and previous. So media bars, status announcements and portal hints on Italian pages are in English. The fr and de tables are about as incomplete (43 and 42 keys).
confirmed.suspectedCause: The partial Italian (and French and German) tables in src/content/i18n.ts fall back to English for most keys.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced on the Corriere article (html lang it-IT, Sift's view lang it-IT). The Sift labels are 'Skip to content', 'Cerca in Corriere', 'Cerca', 'Menu', 'Mostra testo completo', then 'Interactive area from the original page: Example · widget.spreaker.com. Press Enter to use it, Tab to leave.', then 'Vista Sift'. So the skip link and the portal's name and hint are English on an Italian page. The code confirms it. In src/content/i18n.ts, en has 99 keys and it has 42 (fr 43, de 42; he, fa, ru, zh, zh-Hant, ja, ko, tr, nl and pl have 36). t() falls back to en[k] for a missing key. Screen reader users on these pages hear English UI strings: skip, interactive, enterToUse, shortening, shortReady, error, media controls and paging. This breaks 'keeps the page's language' and accessibility on a whole class of pages. Medium.
confirmed.fix: Complete the it, fr and de tables in src/content/i18n.ts (and the 36-key tables) for at least the keys screen readers and status messages use: skip, interactive, enterToUse, the portal hint, shortening, shortReady, error, back10, fwd10, mute, unmute, video, next and previous. A typecheck that makes Table require those keys would stop new gaps.

confirmed.title: Corriere home: Enter in Sift's search sometimes posts the menu form and reloads the home with no results
confirmed.where: https://www.corriere.it/ (Sift header search field, about 10 s after load)
confirmed.evidence: 2 of 4 tries about 9-10 s after load: typing 'Sinner' and pressing Enter sent 'NAV POST https://www.corriere.it/#' and left the home page. The field maps to the burger form (action '#', method post). The other 2 tries at about 9-11 s, and tries at 15 s and 30 s, went to https://www.corriere.it/ricerca/?q=Sinner, which has 5694 results. Clicking Sift's Cerca button worked at 9 s. The site's own handler (keyup Enter on .js-search-input, or a click on .js-search-button) does window.location.href='https://www.corriere.it/ricerca/?q='+value. On the article page, Enter worked 1 of 1.
confirmed.repro: D=/tmp/claude-1001/-home-nico/aac11194-acaf-4dad-a334-0620115b1898/scratchpad/r12t2; SIFT_PORT=9462 SIFT_TAB=T2-news bun $D/drive.ts goto:about:blank netlog goto:https://www.corriere.it/ wait:9000 'sclick:input[type=search]' type:Sinner press:Enter wait:7000 url   (repeat 3-4 times; a failure shows 'NAV POST https://www.corriere.it/#')
confirmed.suspectedCause: Timing in the Enter replay (src/content/proxy.ts key() and submitImplicitly). Sometimes a native submit of the action='#' form wins over the site's keyup or lens-click handler.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced, but at a different time and for a different cause than claimed. 3 of 3 Enter tries at 3-5 s after DOMContentLoaded posted 'NAV POST https://www.corriere.it/#' and left the URL at https://www.corriere.it/#. A click on Sift's Cerca at 4 s did the same. 13 of 13 Enter tries at 7-11 s went to /ricerca/?q=Sinner. I never saw the failure at 9-10 s, though slower loads may push the window later. It is not a race in the Enter replay. Corriere binds its search late. CDP getEventListeners showed no keyup on .js-search-input and no click on .js-search-button until about 11-13 s after navigation start in one run. The load event fired at about 6.4-7.4 s. Before that, the burger form (action '#', method post, button type=submit) is submitted natively, by Chrome's implicit submission for Enter and by the click for Cerca. That only reloads the home and loses the query. In the original, the field sits inside the closed burger menu (left -352) behind the consent wall, so it cannot be used that early. Sift shows a working-looking search at once. Searching in the first seconds, which is realistic, silently does nothing useful. Medium.
confirmed.fix: src/content/proxy.ts submit()/submitImplicitly (or H.act and the Enter path in index.ts): when the form's action is a placeholder ('#', or the current URL with only a fragment) and document.readyState is not 'complete', do not submit natively. Hold the replay until the window load event plus a short delay, then replay Enter or the click. Or show 'loading' on the field until then.

confirmed.verdict: Confirmed, real regression. I rate it high to medium. Harness with a bundle I built from the current src, on fx/r12rx-aspnet.html: 'search: Search products btn=Search more=[Add to cart, Add to wish list, Subscribe]'. The content forms are 'fields=[number:Quantity] actions=[]' and 'fields=[email:Email] actions=[]'. r10m keeps 'actions=[Add to cart; Add to wish list]' and 'actions=[Subscribe]'. In the real extension (port 9468), the top bar is Search box | Search | Add to cart | Add to wish list | Subscribe | Menu | My account. The search input is 50 px wide, so its placeholder and any query are unreadable (shot research/shots/sk12-aspnet.png). The product and the newsletter have no buttons in the content. The cause is as stated: generic.ts:6619 `more` takes every visible submit with an explicit type in pick.form, and here that form is the whole page. I found no live or snapshot page that hits it (no __VIEWSTATE among the snapshots). The pattern is standard for ASP.NET WebForms and JSF pages, though. I did not click the moved buttons, because the hard rules forbid posting forms.
confirmed.fix: src/content/extract/generic.ts findSearch, the `more` filter (line 6619): take only the extra submits that sit inside the smallest ancestor holding both pick and btn (here <header>), with no other visible text field in that ancestor. Or skip `more` when pick.form holds other visible inputs, selects or textareas besides the box. MoinMoin's search form (F1101) still passes either test.

confirmed.title: Pricing cells that two plans share are dropped at narrow widths and zoom when the comparison row scrolls sideways (new offscreen rule in stripCopies)

The snapshots plus live BBC, The Verge and Infobae lose nothing to this rule at 640 px.
